common_diseases.name: Fusarium head blight
common_diseases.symptoms: Bleached, shriveled kernels and pinkish fungal growth on heads
common_diseases.treatment: Apply fungicides at flowering; use resistant varieties

common_diseases.name: Powdery mildew
common_diseases.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems
common_diseases.treatment: Sulfur-based fungicides; ensure good air circulation

common_diseases.name: Leaf rust
common_diseases.treatment: Apply rust-resistant cultivars and timely fungicide sprays

common_pests.name: Aphids
common_pests.treatment: Introduce natural predators; use insecticidal soaps

common_pests.name: Hessian fly
common_pests.treatment: Plant resistant varieties; monitor and apply targeted insecticides

common_pests.name: Wheat midge
common_pests.treatment: Early sowing and insecticide applications during adult emergence

fertilizer.recommended: Apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer at tillering and booting stages

recommendations.irrigation: Maintain soil moisture deficit of 20-30%; avoid water stress during flowering
recommendations.fertilizer: Split nitrogen applications: 50% at sowing, rest at tillering and booting
recommendations.harvesting: Harvest when grain moisture is 12-14% using combine harvester with low grain loss settings
recommendations.storage: Store in ventilated silos at 12-15°C and 60% relative humidity

summary: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a globally important annual cereal grown on loamy to clay soils with pH 6.0-7.5. Optimal temperatures are 10-25 °C, rainfall 300-900 mm/year, and sunlight 6-10 h/day. It requires medium water and nitrogen, with critical moisture needs during flowering. Major producers include China, India, Russia, the United States, and France. Typical yields are 3 t/ha, reaching up to 7 t/ha under optimal management. Key diseases are Fusarium head blight, powdery mildew, and leaf rust; main pests include aphids, Hessian fly, and wheat midge. Integrated pest management, split nitrogen fertilization, and timely harvest ensure high quality grain.
